sources.snippet: Sep 12, 2026 · What is the EU AI Act? The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is the world's first comprehensive horizontal legal framework for artificial intelligence. It entered into force on 1 August 2024 and applies progressively across four risk tiers. The Act uses a risk-based approach: the higher the potential harm, the stricter the obligations.

answer:
The EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) entered into force on 1 August 2024 and applies progressively [5]. The prohibitions, definitions and AI-literacy rules became applicable on 2 February 2025 [1]. Governance rules and obligations for general-purpose AI models took effect on 2 August 2025 [1][3].

On 2 August 2026 the Act became generally applicable: Article 50 transparency duties for chatbots, deepfakes and AI-generated content applied, and the AI Office and national authorities began enforcing it [3][5]. A further ban on AI systems generating non-consensual intimate imagery or child sexual abuse material takes effect on 2 December 2026 [5][6]. Obligations for high-risk systems listed in Annex III apply from 2 December 2027, and obligations for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products (Annex I) apply from 2 August 2028 [1][2][5]. The maximum fine for prohibited practices is €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover [5].
